# PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS] Contents of this Part

## Scope of this Part and definitions

## 57.1

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (1) This Part contains rules about –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (a) probate claims;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (b) claims for the rectification of wills;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (c) claims and applications to –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (i) substitute another person for a personal representative; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (ii) remove a personal representative;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (d) claims under the Inheritance (Provision for Family Dependents) Act 1975(3);

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (e) proceedings under the Presumption of Death Act 2013 1 and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (f) proceedings under the Guardianship (Missing Persons) Act 2017. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (2) In this Part:

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (a) ‘probate claim‘ means a claim for –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (i) the grant of probate of the will, or letters of administration of the estate, of a deceased person;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (ii) the revocation of such a grant; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (iii) a decree pronouncing for or against the validity of an alleged will;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] not being a claim which is non-contentious (or common form) probate business;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (Section 128 of the Supreme Court Act 1981 2 defines non-contentious (or common form) probate business.)

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (b) ‘relevant office’ means –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (i) in the case of High Court proceedings in a Chancery district registry, that registry;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (ii) in the case of any other High Court proceedings, Chancery Chambers at the Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London, WC2A 2LL; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (iii) in the case of County Court proceedings, the office of the County Court hearing centre in question;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (c) ‘testamentary document’ means a will, a draft of a will, written instructions for a will made by or at the request of, or under the instructions of, the testator, and any document purporting to be evidence of the contents, or to be a copy, of a will which is alleged to have been lost or destroyed;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.1] (d) ‘will’ includes a codicil. ## I PROBATE CLAIMS

## General

## 57.2

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.2] (1) This Section contains rules about probate claims. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.2] (2) Probate claims in the High Court are assigned to the Chancery Division. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.2] (3) Probate claims in the County Court must only be started by sending the claim to, or making the claim at –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.2] (a) a County Court hearing centre where there is also a Chancery district registry; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.2] (b) the County Court at Central London. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.2] (4) All probate claims are allocated to the multi-track. ## How to start a probate claim

## 57.3 A probate claim must be commenced –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.3 A probate claim must be commenced –] (a) in the relevant office; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.3 A probate claim must be commenced –] (b) using the procedure in Part 7. ## Acknowledgment of Service and Defence

## 57.4

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.4] (1) A defendant who is served with a claim form must file an acknowledgment of service. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.4] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), the period for filing an acknowledgment of service is –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.4] (a) if the defendant is served with a claim form which states that particulars of claim are to follow, 28 days after service of the particulars of claim; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.4] (b) in any other case, 28 days after service of the claim form. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.4] (3) If the claim form is served out of the jurisdiction under rule 6.32 or 6.33, the period for filing an acknowledgment of service is 14 days longer than the relevant period specified in rule 6.35 or Practice Direction 6B. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.4] (4) Rule 15(4) (which provides the period for filing a defence) applies as if the words ‘under Part 10’ were omitted from rule 15.4(1)(b). ## Lodging of testamentary documents and filing of evidence about testamentary documents

## 57.5

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (1) Any testamentary document of the deceased person in the possession or control of any party must be lodged with the court. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (2) Unless the court directs otherwise, the testamentary documents must be lodged in the relevant office –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (a) by the claimant when the claim form is issued; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (b) by a defendant when he acknowledges service. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (3) The claimant and every defendant who acknowledges service of the claim form must in written evidence –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (a) describe any testamentary document of the deceased of which he has any knowledge or, if he does not know of any such testamentary document, state that fact, and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (b) if any testamentary document of which he has knowledge is not in his possession or under his control, give the name and address of the person in whose possession or under whose control it is or, if he does not know the name or address of that person, state that fact. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (A specimen form for the written evidence about testamentary documents is annexed to Practice Direction 57.)

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (4) Unless the court directs otherwise, the written evidence required by paragraph (3) must be filed in the relevant office –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (a) by the claimant, when the claim form is issued; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (b) by a defendant when he acknowledges service. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (5) Except with the permission of the court, a party shall not be allowed to inspect the testamentary documents or written evidence lodged or filed by any other party until he himself has lodged his testamentary documents and filed his evidence. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.5] (6) The provisions of paragraphs (2) and (4) may be modified by a practice direction under this Part. ## Revocation of existing grant

## 57.6

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.6] (1) In a probate claim which seeks the revocation of a grant of probate or letters of administration every person who is entitled, or claims to be entitled, to administer the estate under that grant must be made a party to the claim. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.6] (2) If the claimant is the person to whom the grant was made, he must lodge the probate or letters of administration in the relevant office when the claim form is issued. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.6] (3) If a defendant has the probate or letters of administration under his control, he must lodge it in the relevant office when he acknowledges service. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.6] (4) Paragraphs (2) and (3) do not apply where the grant has already been lodged at the court, which in this paragraph includes the Principal Registry of the Family Division or a district probate registry. ## Contents of statements of case

## 57.7

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (1) The claim form must contain a statement of the nature of the interest of the claimant and of each defendant in the estate. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (2) If a party disputes another party’s interest in the estate he must state this in his statement of case and set out his reasons. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (3) Any party who contends that at the time when a will was executed the testator did not know of and approve its contents must give particulars of the facts and matters relied on. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (4) Any party who wishes to contend that –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (a) a will was not duly executed;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (b) at the time of the execution of a will the testator lacked testamentary capacity; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (c) the execution of a will was obtained by undue influence or fraud,

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] must set out the contention specifically and give particulars of the facts and matters relied on. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (5)

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (a) A defendant may give notice in his defence that he does not raise any positive case, but insists on the will being proved in solemn form and, for that purpose, will cross-examine the witnesses who attested the will. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.7] (b) If a defendant gives such a notice, the court will not make an order for costs against him unless it considers that there was no reasonable ground for opposing the will. ## Counterclaim

## 57.8

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.8] (1) A defendant who contends that he has any claim or is entitled to any remedy relating to the grant of probate of the will, or letters of administration of the estate, of the deceased person must serve a counterclaim making that contention. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.8] (2) If the claimant fails to serve particulars of claim within the time allowed, the defendant may, with the permission of the court, serve a counterclaim and the probate claim shall then proceed as if the counterclaim were the particulars of claim. ## Probate counterclaim in other proceedings

## 57.9

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.9] (1) In this rule ‘probate counterclaim’ means a counterclaim in any claim other than a probate claim by which the defendant claims any such remedy as is mentioned in rule 57.1(2)(a). [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.9] (2 Subject to the following paragraphs of this rule, this Part shall apply with the necessary modifications to a probate counterclaim as it applies to a probate claim. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.9] (3) A probate counterclaim must contain a statement of the nature of the interest of each of the parties in the estate of the deceased to which the probate counterclaim relates. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.9] (4) Unless an application notice is issued within 7 days after the service of a probate counterclaim for an order under rule 3.1(2)(e) or 3.4 for the probate counterclaim to be dealt with in separate proceedings or to be struck out, and the application is granted, the court will order the transfer of the proceedings to either –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.9] (a) the Chancery Division (if it is not already assigned to that Division) and to either the Royal Courts of Justice or a Chancery district registry (if it is not already proceeding in one of those places); or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.9] (b) if the County Court has jurisdiction, to a County Court hearing centre where there is also a Chancery District Registry or the County Court at Central London. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.9] (5) If an order is made that a probate counterclaim be dealt with in separate proceedings, the order shall order the transfer of the probate counterclaim as required under paragraph (4). ## Failure to acknowledge service or to file a defence

## 57.10

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.10] (1) A default judgment cannot be obtained in a probate claim and rule 10.2 and Part 12 do not apply. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.10] (2) If any of several defendants fails to acknowledge service the claimant may –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.10] (a) after the time for acknowledging service has expired; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.10] (b) upon filing written evidence of service of the claim form and (if no particulars of claim were contained in or served with the claim form) the particulars of claim on that defendant;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.10] proceed with the probate claim as if that defendant had acknowledged service. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.10] (3) If no defendant acknowledges service or files a defence then, unless on the application of the claimant the court orders the claim to be discontinued, the claimant may, after the time for acknowledging service or for filing a defence (as the case may be) has expired, apply to the court for an order that the claim is to proceed to trial. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.10] (4) When making an application under paragraph (3) the claimant must file written evidence of service of the claim form and (if no particulars of claim were contained in or served with the claim form) the particulars of claim on each of the defendants. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.10] (5) Where the court makes an order under paragraph (3), it may direct that the claim be tried on written evidence. ## Discontinuance and dismissal

## 57.11

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.11] (1) Part 38 does not apply to probate claims. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.11] (2) At any stage of a probate claim the court, on the application of the claimant or of any defendant who has acknowledged service, may order that –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.11] (a) the claim be discontinued or dismissed on such terms as to costs or otherwise as it thinks just; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.11] (b) a grant of probate of the will, or letters of administration of the estate, of the deceased person be made to the person entitled to the grant. ## II RECTIFICATION OF WILLS

## Rectification of Wills

## 57.12

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.12] (1) This Section contains rules about claims for the rectification of a will. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.12] (Section 20 of the Administration of Justice Act 1982 3 provides for rectification of a will. Additional provisions are contained in rule 55 of the Non-Contentious Probate Rules 1987 4 . )

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.12] (2) Every personal representative of the estate shall be joined as a party. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.12] (3) Practice Direction 57 makes provision for lodging the grant of probate or letters of administration with the will annexed in a claim under this Section. ## III SUBSTITUTION AND REMOVAL OF PERSONAL REPRESENTATIVES

## Substitution and Removal of Personal Representatives

## 57.13

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.13] (1) This Section contains rules about claims and applications for substitution or removal of a personal representative. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.13] (2) Claims under this Section must be brought in the High Court and are assigned to the Chancery Division. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.13] (Section 50 of the Administration of Justice Act 1985 5 gives the High Court power to appoint a substitute for, or to remove, a personal representative.)

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.13] (3) Every personal representative of the estate shall be joined as a party. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.13] (4) Practice Direction 57 makes provision for lodging the grant of probate or letters of administration in a claim under this Section. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.13] (5) If substitution or removal of a personal representative is sought by application in existing proceedings, this rule shall apply with references to claims being read as if they referred to applications. ## IV CLAIMS UNDER THE INHERITANCE (PROVISION FOR FAMILY AND DEPENDANTS) ACT 1975

## Scope of this section

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > Scope of this section] 57.14 This Section contains rules about claims under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975 6 (‘the Act’). ## Proceedings in the High Court

## 57.15

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.15] (1) Proceedings in the High Court under the Act shall be issued in either –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.15] (a) the Chancery Division; or

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.15] (b) the Family Division. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.15] (2) The Civil Procedure Rules apply to proceedings under the Act which are brought in the Family Division, except that the provisions of the Family Proceedings Rules 2010 7 relating to the drawing up and service of orders apply instead of the provisions in Part 40 and Practice Direction 40B. ## Procedure for claims under section 1 of the Act

## 57.16

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (1) A claim under section 1 of the Act must be made by issuing a claim form in accordance with Part 8. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (2) Rule 8.3 (acknowledgment of service) and rule 8.5 (filing and serving written evidence) apply as modified by paragraphs (3) to (5) of this rule. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (3) The written evidence filed and served by the claimant with the claim form must, except in the circumstances specified in paragraph (3A), have exhibited to it an official copy of –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (a) the grant of probate or letters of administration in respect of the deceased’s estate; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (b) every testamentary document in respect of which probate or letters of administration were granted. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (3A) Where no grant has been obtained, the claimant may make a claim without naming a defendant and may apply for directions as to the representation of the estate. The written evidence must—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (a) explain the reasons why it has not been possible for a grant to be obtained;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (b) be accompanied by the original or a copy (if either is available) of the will or other testamentary document in respect of which probate or letters of administration are to be granted; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (c) contain the following information, so far as known to the claimant—

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (i) brief details of the property comprised in the estate, with an approximate estimate of its capital value and any income that is received from it;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (ii) brief details of the liabilities of the estate;

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (iii) the names and addresses of the persons who are in possession of the documents relating to the estate; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (iv) the names of the beneficiaries and their respective interests in the estate. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (3B) Where a claim is made in accordance with paragraph (3A), the court may give directions as to the parties to the claim and as to the representation of the estate either on the claimant’s application or on its own initiative. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (Section 4 of the 1975 Act as amended confirms that nothing prevents the making of an application under the Act before representation with respect to the estate of the deceased person is taken out.)

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (4) Subject to paragraph (4A), the time within which a defendant must file and serve –

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (a) an acknowledgment of service; and

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (b) any written evidence,

[PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] is not more than 21 days after service of the claim form on him. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (4A) If the claim form is served out of the jurisdiction under rule 6.32 or 6.33, the period for filing an acknowledgment of service and any written evidence is 7 days longer than the relevant period specified in rule 6.35 or Practice Direction 6B. [PART 57 – PROBATE, INHERITANCE, PRESUMPTION OF DEATH AND GUARDIANSHIP OF MISSING PERSONS > 57.16] (5) A defendant who is a personal representative of the deceased must file and serve written evidence, which must include the information required by Practice Direction 57. ## V PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PRESUMPTION OF DEATH ACT 2013
